PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single requirement/behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make failures easy to diagnose. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if exactly one method call / one scenario is tested; non-compliant if multiple Act operations or multiple unrelated behaviors are exercised. DECISION RULES: 1) Count distinct Act operations. 2) Check test name for multiple operations. 3) If single call and single assertion group, compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the method performs multiple distinct acts: it constructs a MaxMin4 instance (constructor check) and separately invokes MaxMin4.maxMin4(sample, 0, sample.length - 1). These are two distinct behaviors (construction and a static method invocation) within the same test, thus violating atomicity.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent and not rely on each other's state. RATIONALE: Independence allows reordering and parallel execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Before/@After or lack of shared mutable state. DECISION RULES: 1) Check for lifecycle annotations. 2) Check for shared mutable instance/static fields modified by tests. 3) If only local variables are used, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — test2 uses only local variables and does not reference or mutate static/instance fields or rely on other tests; there are no lifecycle methods required here.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should cover happy paths and error/exceptional scenarios. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and correct error handling. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if for each method there are at least two tests (happy path and error case) or explicit assertThrows/@Test(expected=...). DECISION RULES: 1) If all tests only use valid inputs and expect success, non-compliant. 2) Look for @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows; if present, lean compliant. 3) Look for test names indicating error scenarios. 4) If class has < 2 tests, likely only happy path -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant — the class contains a single test that tries a call inside a try/catch but does not provide explicit tests for exceptional flows (no assertThrows or @Test(expected=...)). The try/catch swallows ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and does not assert error behavior, so exceptional cases are not explicitly covered.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should exercise boundary values (min, max, just inside/outside). RATIONALE: Many bugs occur at boundaries. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for use of 0, -1, empty, sample.length-1, etc. DECISION RULES: 1) If test data contains 0 or sample.length-1, lean compliant. 2) Names indicating edge tests also count. 3) If only typical values used, non-compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the test explicitly invokes MaxMin4.maxMin4(sample, 0, sample.length - 1), exercising index boundaries (0 and length-1), which are key boundary indices for array-based methods.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helper methods/constants. RATIONALE: Modularity reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for helper methods, constants, or lack of duplication. DECISION RULES: 1) If helper methods/constants exist, lean compliant. 2) If identical code repeats in multiple tests, non-compliant. 3) If tests are short and no repetition exists, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — there is no duplicated code across multiple tests (only one test exists) and the test is self-contained; therefore modularity concerns are minimal for this method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and with low cyclomatic complexity. RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to maintain and less error-prone. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if method length < 20 and no loops/complex conditionals; non-compliant if > 30 lines or contains loops/branches. DECISION RULES: 1) If any test > 30 lines, non-compliant. 2) If loops/complex conditionals present, non-compliant. 3) If linear short flow, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — test2 is a relatively short, linear test without loops or nested conditional logic, so complexity is low.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple relevant properties to detect faults. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may miss defects. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test verifies multiple properties of results or objects. DECISION RULES: 1) If only one superficial assertion, non-compliant. 2) If >=2 property checks for returned objects, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the test asserts both non-null construction and exact runtime class (two properties) for the created instance, which verifies multiple aspects of construction.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not be ignored or commented-out. RATIONALE: Ignored tests provide no value and hide problems. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: 1) If @Ignore/@Disabled present, non-compliant. 2) If commented-out tests present, non-compliant. 3) Otherwise compliant. VERDICT: compliant — there are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations and no commented-out @Test methods in the provided class; the test is active.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be linked to requirements. RATIONALE: Traceability helps maintain coverage and debugging. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if class/method doc or annotations reference requirement IDs. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for @Story/@Requirement or Javadoc with REQ-/US- IDs. 2) If present, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the class Javadoc explicitly references requirements (REQ-004 and REQ-010), providing traceability.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests should be explicit and separate. RATIONALE: Non-functional behavior needs dedicated tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if explicit performance tests exist (e.g., @Test(timeout=...)) or explicit security checks. DECISION RULES: 1) Usually not-applicable for unit tests. 2) Mark compliant if @Test(timeout=...) present. 3) Mark non-compliant if class name suggests performance tests but none present. VERDICT: compliant — the test method is annotated with @Test(timeout = 4000), which is an explicit timing constraint indicating a performance-related assertion (JUnit timeout), so this practice is considered satisfied for this method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should have descriptive names indicating scenario and expected result. RATIONALE: Good names make tests self-documenting. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if names follow patterns like method_condition_expectedBehavior. DECISION RULES: 1) If names follow descriptive patterns, compliant. 2) If names are generic (test1, test2), non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant — the test method is named 'test2', a generic autogenerated-style name that does not describe scenario or expected outcome, so it fails the naming clarity requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Generated tests should be minimal and intention-revealing. RATIONALE: Verbose auto-generated tests are hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if there are signs of heavy auto-generation (auto-generated comments, generic names like test0/test1, EvoSuite artifacts). DECISION RULES: 1) Look for 'Auto-generated by...' comments or EvoSuite artifacts. 2) Look for repetitive generic names. 3) If no signs, mark not-applicable. VERDICT: non-compliant — the presence of imports from org.evosuite.runtime and the generic method name 'test2' indicate the test originated from an auto-generation tool (EvoSuite) and retains autogenerated naming/patterns, which is a sign of heavy code generation rather than small focused produced tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should be designed with clear intent (Given-When-Then, BDD or TDD). RATIONALE: Thoughtful design leads to comprehensive coverage. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming present or tests cover multiple scenarios. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for Given-When-Then comments. 2) If multiple scenarios covered, compliant. 3) If only minimal tests, non-compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the test contains explicit 'Given / When' and 'Then' comments and class-level requirement notes, indicating a deliberate design approach and prioritization for the behaviors under test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should target public behavior, not internal implementation details. RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are less brittle. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use only public APIs and do not use reflection or inspect private fields. DECISION RULES: 1) If reflection is used, non-compliant. 2) If tests inspect internal private state, non-compliant. 3) Otherwise, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the test uses public constructor and static public method calls and does not use reflection or verify private/internal state; it tests observable behavior through public API.

PRINCIPLE: Use specific assertions and descriptive messages to make failures diagnosable. RATIONALE: Clear assertions speed debugging. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if assertions use assertEquals/assertNotNull with messages rather than generic assertTrue. DECISION RULES: 1) If assertions include messages and use specific methods, compliant. 2) If only assertTrue used where assertEquals would be better, non-compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the test uses assertNotNull and assertEquals with descriptive messages and uses fail(...) with a message on unexpected exceptions, meeting the criteria for clear, specific assertions.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain why, not what, and be minimal. RATIONALE: Useful comments help future maintainers without clutter. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if comments are informative (Given-When-Then) and no commented-out code. DECISION RULES: 1) If commented-out code present, non-compliant. 2) If >50% of lines are comments, non-compliant. 3) Otherwise, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the method includes concise Given/When/Then comments that describe intent and no commented-out code or excessive commenting, so comments add value rather than clutter.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be deterministic and avoid randomness/time dependencies. RATIONALE: Deterministic tests avoid flakiness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no Random, System.currentTimeMillis, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies without mocks. DECISION RULES: 1) If Random()/currentTime used without mocking, non-compliant. 2) If Thread.sleep used, non-compliant. 3) Otherwise, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the test uses fixed sample input and deterministic calls; there is no use of Random, time-based functions, sleeps, or external dependencies, so it is deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid modifying global/shared state and should clean up resources. RATIONALE: Avoids inter-test interference. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no persistent side effects or static modifications and if cleanup is present when needed. DECISION RULES: 1) If @After/@AfterEach cleanup present, lean compliant. 2) If file/database writes without cleanup, non-compliant. 3) If only local variables used, compliant. VERDICT: compliant — test2 uses only local variables and does not create files, databases, or modify static state; there are no side effects to clean up.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/tags/categories to organize tests. RATIONALE: Facilitates selective runs and CI efficiency. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Tag/@Category/@Category annotations present with meaningful labels. DECISION RULES: 1) If @Tag/@Category present, compliant. 2) If no categorization at all, non-compliant. 3) If class tiny (1-2 tests), not-applicable. VERDICT: compliant — the class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) which provides meaningful categorization for unit tests, satisfying the practice.
